concept.name: Circuit Breakers & Resilience Patterns
concept.tagline: Prevent cascading microservice outages by tripping circuit breakers when downstream failure thresholds are breached.

spark.summary: Circuit Breakers monitor remote service call failure rates. If downstream failures exceed a threshold (e.g. 50%), the breaker trips to OPEN, instantly returning fallback responses instead of stalling threads.
spark.keyTakeaway: Use Closed → Open → Half-Open state transitions to fail fast and automatically recover.

concept.whyItMatters: A slow downstream payment gateway blocks API threads across the entire microservice mesh, triggering a total outage.
whenToUse: Microservice HTTP calls to third-party APIs.
keyPoints: Closed State: Normal operation; tracks failure rates.
Open State: Tripped; short-circuits requests immediately to fallback.
Half-Open State: Allows trial requests to test downstream recovery.

deepDive.markdownContent:
## 📖 State Machine: Closed, Open, and Half-Open

The circuit breaker pattern wraps remote network interactions in a stateful proxy that acts as an automatic safety switch. When downstream services degrade, the breaker short-circuits calls to prevent thread pool exhaustion, latency spikes, and cluster-wide cascading failures.

```architecture
{
  "view": "high-level",
  "title": "Circuit Breaker State Machine & Flow",
  "nodes": [
    { "id": "client", "label": "Caller Service", "type": "client" },
    { "id": "breaker", "label": "Circuit Breaker (Proxy)", "type": "service" },
    { "id": "remote", "label": "Downstream API", "type": "database" },
    { "id": "fallback", "label": "Fallback Response", "type": "processor" }
  ],
  "edges": [
    { "from": "client", "to": "breaker", "label": "1. Invoke Call" },
    { "from": "breaker", "to": "remote", "label": "2a. Normal Flow (Closed)" },
    { "from": "breaker", "to": "fallback", "label": "2b. Short-Circuit (Open)" }
  ]
}
```

### ⚙️ The Three Core States & Transition Rules

The circuit breaker transitions through three deterministic operational states based on sliding window failure metrics:

1. **CLOSED (Normal Operation)**
   - Inbound requests pass through unimpeded to the remote service.
   - The breaker maintains a rolling window of recent calls (e.g. the last 100 requests or past 10 seconds).
   - If the failure rate (5xx errors, timeouts, or slow calls > 500ms) crosses `failureRateThreshold` (typically 50%) **and** call volume exceeds `minimumNumberOfCalls` (e.g. 20), the breaker trips to **OPEN**.

2. **OPEN (Short-Circuit & Fail-Fast)**
   - Inbound requests are immediately intercepted with a fast failure (`CallNotPermittedException`) without placing network load on the downstream service.
   - Callers execute configured fallback logic (cached responses, default values, or graceful degradation).
   - Downstream systems receive zero traffic, giving them the CPU and DB headroom needed to recover.
   - The breaker remains OPEN for a configured cooldown timer (`waitDurationInOpenState`, typically 10–30s). When expired, it transitions to **HALF-OPEN**.

3. **HALF-OPEN (Canary Health Probe)**
   - A limited batch of trial canary calls (`permittedNumberOfCallsInHalfOpenState`, e.g. 10 calls) is allowed through to test downstream viability.
   - All excess requests arriving during the trial window are still short-circuited to fallback.
   - If the trial batch failure rate stays below threshold, downstream recovery is confirmed: the breaker transitions back to **CLOSED** and resets error counters.
   - If any trial calls fail, the breaker snaps immediately back to **OPEN** and restarts the cooldown timer.

### 📊 Sliding Window Counting Mechanics

Production libraries like Resilience4j and Envoy implement sliding windows to ensure statistical stability:

| Window Type | Mechanism | Memory Overhead | Best Used For |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Count-based** | Circular ring buffer of $N$ measurements (e.g. 100 calls) | Constant $O(1)$ space | Consistent, high-QPS services |
| **Time-based** | Bucketed epoch ring (e.g. 10 buckets of 1 second each) | Prunes oldest bucket per second | Bursty or sporadic traffic |

### 🛡️ Why Circuit Breakers Must Pair with Bulkheads

A circuit breaker alone cannot protect thread pools from saturation during the window before the threshold is breached. Always pair circuit breakers with **Bulkheads** (thread pool isolation or semaphore limits) so that an unresponsive third-party integration cannot consume thread pools dedicated to critical authentication or checkout workflows.

questions.title: Circuit Breaker State Machine Transitions
questions.prompt: In a Circuit Breaker state machine (Closed, Open, Half-Open), what triggers the transition from OPEN back to HALF-OPEN?

options.text: The downstream service sends a manual HTTP POST webhook to reset the breaker.
options.explanation: Circuit breakers use automated timers rather than external webhooks to transition states.

options.text: An evaluation cooldown timer expires, allowing a small canary probe of trial requests to test downstream health.
options.explanation: Correct! Expiration of the open cooldown timer moves the breaker to Half-Open to test trial requests.

rubric.excellent: Explains expiration of cooldown window and trial request probing in Half-Open state.
rubric.gap: Thinks manual restart is required.

questions.sampleSolution: After the open cooldown timer expires, the breaker transitions to Half-Open to send trial requests to test recovery.
questions.explanation: Half-Open acts as a safety probe before returning the breaker to full Closed operation.

interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: Your e-commerce backend integrates with Stripe and PayPal for payment processing. During a payment partner outage, latency spikes from 200ms to 30 seconds per request, causing app server thread pool exhaustion. How do you protect overall checkout availability?
constraints: App server thread pool size: 200 workers.

dimensions.description: Tripping circuit breaker OPEN to instantly fail fast or route to fallback.

interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Wrap payment provider SDK calls in a Resilience4j circuit breaker with a 50% failure threshold and 5-second execution timeout. If Stripe times out, trip to OPEN immediately to route checkouts to PayPal fallback.
commonPitfalls: Allowing workers to block for 30 seconds on timing out calls, starving thread pools.
